title: The Clipper Ship 'Flying Cloud' at Sea Under Full Sail

story.what: McKay's Flying Cloud shown broadside under a full press of canvas, every sail drawing.
story.why: She made New York to San Francisco in 89 days twice, a record under sail that stood for over a century.
story.notice: Count the STUDDING sails booms run out beyond the yards - speed bought with spars.

title: Clipper Ship Comet of New York in a Hurricane off Bermuda
water: off Bermuda, bound for San Francisco

story.what: The Comet laid nearly on her beam ends in the October 1852 hurricane, storm canvas straining.
story.why: Parsons drew disaster survived, not disaster - the print sold the nerve of the trade, not its wrecks.
story.notice: The sea BREAKS clean over the lee rail; the crew are dots, the ship is the hero.

title: Clipper Ship 'Red Jacket' in the Ice off Cape Horn
artist: Currier & Ives (after J. B. Smith & Son, on stone by C. Parsons)
water: off Cape Horn, Australia to Liverpool

story.what: Red Jacket threads a field of Antarctic ice under shortened sail, August 1854.
story.why: She ran Liverpool to New York in 13 days on her maiden passage - the fastest sailing crossing ever recorded.
story.notice: The bergs are drawn ARCHITECTURAL, like ruined cathedrals; the ship keeps her manners among them.

title: Clipper Ship Great Republic

story.what: McKay's four-decked giant, the largest wooden sailing ship ever launched, shown under full sail.
story.why: She burned at her New York pier before her maiden voyage; the print preserves the ship as built, which no photograph could.
story.notice: Four masts on a CLIPPER - the extreme of the type, drawn without apology.

title: Clipper Ship 'Great Republic' - Length on Deck 325 Feet

story.what: The rebuilt Great Republic at sea, her dimensions printed in the title like a boast.
story.why: Currier sold statistics as spectacle - tonnage and beam were parlor conversation in the 1850s.
story.notice: The title block reads like a BROKER'S circular; the image reads like scripture.
story.meaning: Measured in feet, sold in awe.

title: A Clipper Ship in a Hurricane

story.what: An unnamed clipper stripped to storm sail, running before a hurricane sea.
story.why: The generic storm print let every owner's widow and every owner's banker see the same picture differently.
story.notice: No name on the BOW - this ship is every ship, which was the point.

title: New York Clipper Ship 'Challenge'
water: outbound, New York to San Francisco

story.what: The extreme clipper Challenge, sharpest hull of her day, under a cloud of canvas.
story.why: Built to beat every ship afloat, she is remembered for a brutal maiden passage - the print records the promise, not the voyage.
story.notice: The hull drawn KNIFE-thin at the bow; speed was carved before it was sailed.

title: Clipper Ship Three Brothers, 2972 Tons

story.what: The ex-steamer Vanderbilt rerigged as the sailing ship Three Brothers, billed as the largest in the world.
story.why: By 1875 the boast had passed from speed to size - the clipper era ending in tonnage.
story.notice: Look for the HULL of a steamship under sailing rig - an era converted, not built.
story.meaning: Size is what remains of speed.

title: Dreadnought, a Fast Clipper Ship

story.what: The 'Wild Boat of the Atlantic' on the Liverpool run she made famous under Captain Samuels.
story.why: Dreadnought kept packet schedules under sail alone and became a folk song before she became a wreck.
story.notice: The red CROSS on her foretopsail - her private mark, recognized from both shores.

title: Clipper Ship 'Queen of Clippers'

story.what: The Boston-built Queen of Clippers running large, sails set to royals.
story.why: A ship named like a claim - the 1850s market rewarded superlatives in oak as in ink.
story.notice: The name on the STERN does the advertising; the lithographer merely agrees.

title: Clipper Ship Witch of the Wave

story.what: The Portsmouth-built tea clipper that ran Whampoa to Dungeness in 90 days.
story.why: Her record tea passage made an American hull famous in a trade the British thought their own.
story.notice: The FIGUREHEAD - a witch in flowing dress - leans farther forward than the bow itself.

title: Transport Clipper Ocean Express in Tow of the Illinois

story.what: A war artist's sketch of the clipper Ocean Express under tow as a Union transport.
story.why: The war conscripted the clippers; Waud drew the fastest ships afloat reduced to barges behind steam.
story.notice: The towline SAGS - the whole clipper era hangs in that curve.
story.meaning: Steam did not race; it collected.

title: The Clipper Ship Sweepstakes

story.what: The extreme clipper Sweepstakes, holder of the New York to Bombay record, as remembered by Cozzens.
story.why: Painted seventy years after her launch - the clippers were already a memory industry by 1924.
story.notice: A portrait made from RECORDS, not from life; nostalgia drawn rigging-accurate.

title: The Clipper Ship Sea Witch

story.what: The record-breaking Sea Witch as painted by a Chinese port artist for her officers to carry home.
story.why: Her 74-day Canton to New York run was never beaten by a sailing ship; her portraits were painted at both ends of it.
story.notice: A CHINESE hand painted America's fastest ship - the trade ran in both directions.

title: 'Taeping' and 'Ariel' in the Great Tea Race of 1866
water: the English Channel, Foochow to London

story.what: Taeping and Ariel side by side in the Channel after ninety-nine days and sixteen thousand miles from Foochow.
story.why: The 1866 tea race finished with two ships docking twenty minutes apart - the closest ocean race ever sailed.
story.notice: After 99 days the gap between them is a few CABLES - read that against the distance run.

title: Sovereign of the Seas
artist: after a period lithograph (State Street Trust plate)
water: the Australia and San Francisco runs

story.what: McKay's Sovereign of the Seas, the ship that logged 22 knots - the fastest speed ever recorded under sail alone.
story.why: No buyer would order so large a clipper, so McKay built her on his own account and let her passages sell themselves.
story.notice: Reproduced in 1913 from a period print - the clippers entered the history books while men who sailed them LIVED.
story.meaning: He built her on speculation; she paid in legend.

title: Clipper Ship David Crockett - Sailing Card

story.what: A counting-house handbill announcing the David Crockett loading for San Francisco.
story.why: She made twenty-five Cape Horn passages and paid her owners every year - the steadiest earner of the fleet.
story.notice: The card promises DISPATCH - the one word every shipper paid for.

title: Clipper Ship Andrew Jackson - Sailing Card

story.what: The sailing card of the ship that matched Flying Cloud's 89-day record to San Francisco.
story.why: Her 1859-60 run tied the fastest passage ever sailed, and the card was how the wharf found out first.
story.notice: The general's PORTRAIT stands in for the ship - politics sold berths too.

title: Clipper Ship Nightingale - Sailing Card
water: Boston to Australia and the East

story.what: The card of the Nightingale, named for Jenny Lind and carrying her portrait at the bow.
story.why: Launched for the London Exhibition trade, she sailed every trade after - including, darkly, the slave trade before her Navy capture.
story.notice: Named for a SINGER - the 1850s sold ocean passage like an opera ticket.
story.meaning: A voice, a hull, a history.

title: Clipper Ship Great Republic - Sailing Card

story.what: The rebuilt Great Republic advertised for the California run.
story.why: After the fire she sailed cut down a deck - still the largest thing loading on South Street.
story.notice: The type is set LARGE; for this ship no exaggeration was available.

title: Clipper Ship Young America - Sailing Card

story.what: The card of Webb's masterpiece, twenty years on the Cape Horn run.
story.why: Fifty passages around the Horn without a major loss - underwriters quoted her name as a rate.
story.notice: The name is a SLOGAN - the ship, the movement, and the customer were all young America.

title: Clipper Ship Dreadnought - Sailing Card

story.what: The packet clipper Dreadnought's loading card for the Liverpool run.
story.why: Samuels advertised passage times no steamship line dared print - and largely kept them.
story.notice: The card sells a DATE of sailing, not a hope of one - the packet's whole invention.

title: Clipper Ship Hornet - Sailing Card

story.what: The sailing card of the Hornet, famous for a dead-heat race to San Francisco and a fiery end.
story.why: Her 1866 burning and the crew's 43-day open-boat survival gave Mark Twain his first famous story.
story.notice: A STING in the name - job printers picked emblems a stevedore could read at a walk.

title: Clipper Ship Comet - Sailing Card

story.what: The loading card of the Comet, one of the fastest hulls Webb ever drew.
story.why: She beat the record steamer time to California in 1853 - a sailing ship, faster than coal.
story.notice: A comet TAIL streams through the type - Victorian job printing at full stretch.

title: Clipper Ship Ocean Telegraph - Sailing Card

story.what: The card of the Ocean Telegraph, named for the newest wonder of the age.
story.why: Ships were christened for the technology that would retire them - the cable named here made the clipper obsolete.
story.notice: The name honors the WIRE that would put the ship out of work.

title: Clipper Ship Romance of the Sea - Sailing Card

story.what: The card of McKay's sharpest hull, lost with all hands in the China Sea.
story.why: The name was the sales pitch and the epitaph both; she vanished in 1863 without a survivor.
story.notice: The word ROMANCE printed over a freight tariff - the whole era in one card.

title: Clipper Ship Storm King - Sailing Card

story.what: The Storm King's loading notice, crowned with a suitably theatrical monarch of weather.
story.why: Card art turned the voyage's chief hazard into its trademark - the storm, domesticated for the counting house.
story.notice: The king RIDES the gale he is named for; shippers were meant to infer the ship did too.
story.meaning: Sell the storm, book the hold.

title: Clipper Ship Flying Fish - Sailing Card

story.what: The card of McKay's Flying Fish, twice within days of the San Francisco record.
story.why: She and Flying Cloud were stablemates in the great deep-sea derby of 1852 - handbills were the race coverage.
story.notice: The fish FLIES on the card as the ship never quite did - second-fastest, forever.

title: Clipper Ship Herald of the Morning - Sailing Card

story.what: The card of the Herald of the Morning, a 99-day ship on the California run.
story.why: One of the few clippers to break 100 days more than once - a fact every card of hers found room to print.
story.notice: DAWN imagery on a freight notice; the trade woke early and said so.
